{
  "extract_plan": {
    "chunk_summary": "Statistics Canada Quality Guidelines phase 5 (profile and prepare data) enumerates operational guidelines for data examination/editing/cleaning, edit and imputation (including donor imputation and imputation classes), adjustment and reweighting (calibration, weight range control, non‑response weighting classes), assessment/documentation, final processing (survey weights, PUMF, master and shared files), and the phase's quality dimensions and indicators."
  },
  "concepts": [
    {
      "id": "c-donor-imputation",
      "name": "donor imputation",
      "aliases": ["hot-deck imputation"],
      "description": "Imputation approach in which missing values on a recipient record are filled from a donor record; the guidelines recommend a single donor per record, nearest-neighbour selection, and random choice among equidistant donors.",
      "anchor": "In the case of donor imputation",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-auxiliary-variables",
      "name": "auxiliary variables",
      "aliases": ["auxiliary information", "auxiliary data"],
      "description": "Variables drawn from other data sources used to impute missing data, to establish imputation classes, to explain the non-response mechanism, and to calibrate or adjust weights.",
      "anchor": "Explore various data sources",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-imputation-classes",
      "name": "imputation classes",
      "aliases": ["imputation cells"],
      "description": "Groupings of records, established from auxiliary variables, within which imputation is carried out; methods are retested when classes are combined.",
      "anchor": "establish imputation classes",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-non-response-model",
      "name": "non‑response model",
      "aliases": ["nonresponse model"],
      "description": "Model of the non-response mechanism, determined by analyzing characteristics of respondents and non-respondents, used to choose compensation methods and to form weighting classes that guard against its failure.",
      "anchor": "failure of the non‑response model",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-non-response-weighting-classes",
      "name": "non‑response weighting classes",
      "aliases": ["weighting classes"],
      "description": "Classes formed for non-response weighting to strengthen against failure of the non-response model and to avoid extreme weights.",
      "anchor": "Form non‑response weighting classes",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-calibration",
      "name": "calibration",
      "aliases": ["calibration estimation"],
      "description": "Weight adjustment technique to consider when auxiliary data are correlated to the variables of interest, requiring auxiliary data for sampled units and known or accurately estimated population totals.",
      "anchor": "Consider calibration",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-nearest-neighbour-method",
      "name": "nearest‑neighbour method",
      "aliases": ["nearest neighbour donor selection"],
      "description": "Donor-selection method that finds a donor as close as possible to the record to be imputed, using appropriately selected variables to identify the nearest neighbour.",
      "anchor": "Consider the nearest‑neighbour method",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-weight-range-control",
      "name": "weight range control methods",
      "aliases": ["weight trimming"],
      "description": "Methods used to avoid extreme or negative weights during reweighting.",
      "anchor": "Use weight range control methods",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-survey-weights",
      "name": "survey weights",
      "aliases": ["estimation weights"],
      "description": "Weights adjusted to reduce non-response, coverage and sampling errors and added to individual records during final processing, including weights for the shared file.",
      "anchor": "Add survey weights",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-pumf",
      "name": "PUMF",
      "aliases": ["public use microdata file"],
      "description": "Output file for which record identification codes are created and to which new variables may be added as a result of suppressions required to create it.",
      "anchor": "the master file, the PUMF",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-imputation",
      "name": "imputation",
      "aliases": ["missing data imputation"],
      "description": "Compensation for missing data whose degree and effects are to be assessed, whose added variance is to be measured, and whose methods and sources are to be flagged.",
      "anchor": "Assess the degree and effects",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    },
    {
      "id": "c-edit-rules",
      "name": "edit rules",
      "aliases": ["editing rules"],
      "description": "Documented rules for examining and editing acquired data; a guide is to be provided and the work monitored so that the rules are interpreted identically and consistently by all editors.",
      "anchor": "Provide a guide of edit rules",
      "location": "statcan-quality-guidelines-6th-edition#c0017"
    }
  ],
